request_state.literature: Literature (primary source arXiv:2412.11933, survey of solved cases): fully solved with all exponents>=3 are (3,3,n) for n<=10^9, (n,n,3) for n>=3, (n,n,n) for n>=3. Effective-finiteness only (not solved): (2p,2q,r) with p,q>=V_r [arXiv:2509.21083]. NOT solved: (4,4,5), (4,4,7), (4,6,3), any (2m,2n,r odd) with m!=n, (3,5,7), (5,5,7).
request_state.claim: Sharp curvature separation. Every hyperbolic Beal signature has |chi| >= 1/12 with equality exactly at permutations of (3,3,4), while every one of the ten known primitive hyperbolic solutions has |chi| <= 1/18. Hence Beal is equivalent to: no primitive solution has |chi| >= 1/12. This explains the exponent-2 phenomenon quantitatively - an exponent 2 contributes 1/2 to the reciprocal sum, which is what permits |chi| to stay small.
